chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from a man, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa ibn Ukayl al-Numayri, from al-'Ala' ibn Sayabah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: regarding

A confined well into which a man falls and dies in it, and it is not possible to remove him from the well—may wudu (ablution) be performed from that well? He عليه السلام said: 'Wudu (ablution) is not performed from it. It is to be left unused and made a grave. And if it is possible to remove him, he is to be taken out, washed, and buried.
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: 'The sanctity of the Muslim when dead is like his sanctity when alive, equally.'

key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well used as a water source
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: he is to be washed ritually after death
key_terms.مَيِّتًا: in the state of being dead
key_terms.يُعَطَّلُ: it is to be left unused

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using water from a well in which a person has died?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a well in which a person has died. It states that wudu (ablution) should not be performed from such a well if the body cannot be removed, and it emphasizes the sanctity of the deceased Muslim by treating the well as a grave. If removal is possible, the body is to be taken out, given ghusl, and buried properly.
